text: Marcelo Miranda Viana da Silva, born on 4 March 1962 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, is a Brazilian mathematician specializing in chaotic dynamical systems and strange attractors. His parents were Portuguese, and he grew up in Portugal, where he completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Porto. He earned his Ph.D. from the Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada (IMPA) in Rio de Janeiro under the supervision of Jacob Palis. Viana is currently the director of IMPA, a position he was elected to for the period 2016–2019. He proved the Zorich–Kontsevich conjecture in collaboration with Artur Avila. In 1993, he was awarded a Guggenheim Fellowship. He received the TWAS Prize in 1998 and the inaugural ICTP Ramanujan Prize in 2005 for his research achievements. Viana served as vice-president of the International Mathematical Union from 2011 to 2014 and as president of the Brazilian Mathematical Society from 2013 to 2015. In 1998, he delivered a plenary lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Berlin. He chaired the executive committee for the 2018 International Congress of Mathematicians held in Rio de Janeiro and is a columnist for Folha de S.Paulo.
